answer: One concrete defense is per-agent proof of standalone history: each agent must accumulate verifiable, paid interactions that no other identity shares. A Sybil swarm born on one island of identical scripts looks uniform, so peers weight an agent by its distinct counterparties and settled volume, not headcount. A new cluster stranded on the mesa of zero history owns no ridge of proven deals, and forging that record costs the attacker real capital and time per identity, scaling linearly with every fake node instead of once. Cheap mass identity therefore buys almost no voting or trust weight.
